recfVFnXBwRsp6WLY.Bio: Steven A. Young holds an MSci and a PhD in theoretical physics, and now describes himself as an author, musician and natural philosopher. He is the author of A Fool's Wisdom: Science Conspiracies & The Secret Art of Alchemy, which critiques scientific materialism before presenting Hermetic alchemy as a science of transformation. Under the alias Hedflux he has produced electronic music since 2003, going full time in 2010 and founding the label Luminus Music, with a body of work collected in a 20 Year Legacy Collection of 88 tracks and 12 DJ mixes. He lives in Scotland, where he teaches Audio Alchemy, a synthesis of musical, scientific and Hermetic knowledge.
recfVFnXBwRsp6WLY.Name: Steven Young

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Atomism's Sketchy Pedigree and Aristotle's Answer", "body": "Young traces atomism back to Leucippus, of whom no writings survive, then to his supposed student Democritus, the laughing philosopher, and on to Epicurus and the hedonism of Epicureanism. He notes a Roman author around 100 to 50 BC revived the Greek atomists, and questions whether those Greeks were written into history at all. Aristotle, by contrast, left extensive writings, opposed atomism, and taught four elements plus ether, a paradigm Young says stood worldwide for two thousand years until the atomic revival of the 1600s. Aristotle's objection, Young contends, is that matter is continuous and infinitely divisible, with no smallest part."}, {"title": "Alchemy as Hands-On Science You Can Practice at Home", "body": "Chance opens the alchemy discussion by reading from Young's book A Fool's Wisdom, which contrasts the abstract models and postulated particles of academia with a science of real sensory phenomena you can apply at home. Young, a theoretical physicist by training, says the symbolism went over his head at first, but the physics of alchemy made immediate sense, since fire, water and earth can be sensed, measured and built with. He describes the seven processes, drying, dissolving, combining, fermenting, and his wife making hydrosols and balms from garden herbs. Chance cites Godfrey Higgins in Anacalypsis on Locke's doctrine that no idea arrives except through the senses."}, {"title": "Fire, the Salamander and the Grammar of the Elements", "body": "Asked about the generative power, Young assigns it to fire, whose spirits are the salamander, which regrows its limbs and organs and so embodies regeneration, and the dragon, which carries fire's destructive side. Fire is called the great mover because it penetrates every substance. He maps nigredo, the reduction to black ash, and the whitening that follows it, onto ordeals like the dark night of the soul, noting how close heat sits to hate. The qualities carry the rest: fire hot and dry, air warm and wet, earth cold and dry, water cold and wet. The two men then trace fire through slang like stoked, lit and buzz kill."}, {"title": "Water, the Sealed Terrarium and What the Periodic Table Sorts", "body": "Young argues the periodic table's 118 elements amount to a ranking by density, since atomic mass is itself calculated from the observable density, and that its chemical elements are purified substances rather than the impure, readily available elements of alchemy. He contends hydrogen and oxygen are produced from water by running electricity through it, not the reverse. He suspects the realm holds a fixed amount of water, citing David Latimer's terrarium, sealed in 1960 and topped up only once in 1972, still thriving. Chance raises his AquaCure electrolysis device, George Wiseman's unexplained sludge, primary water claims, mud floods and deluge lore."}, {"title": "From Roughness to Medi-Sin, Living by the Elemental Framework", "body": "Young credits Mandelbrot's obsession with roughness, a quality he says belongs uniquely to earth, for showing that rock looks the same at every scale, which he ties back to Aristotle's continuous matter. He introduces hylomorphism, hylo for matter and morphe for form, as Aristotle's alternative to atoms and molecules. Young says he feels far more secure understanding his body as fire, air, earth and water than as trillions of atoms, and both men play with sign, sine and medi-sin as bringing things back to center. Chance's outro adds the al and kimia etymology, the five senses mapped to the elements, and every power source traced to one of the four."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Steven Young is the author of "A Fool's Wisdom" and creator of Hedflux. In his second InnerVerse appearance, Steven brings a lively revival of knowledge, including the forgotten gnosis expressed by alchemy's quintessential elements. Topics include practical alchemical applications for life, elemental qualities and the encoding within their respective symbols, refuting the periodic table and atomism, and a lot more.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this second conversation with Steven Young, author of A Fool's Wisdom, InnerVerse dives into the alchemy half of his book: why alchemy deals in real sensory phenomena while atomism deals in abstractions, how 2,000 years of Aristotelian elemental physics formed the worldwide scientific consensus until the 17th-century atomic revival, the fire element as the Great Mover and the salamander as its generative spirit, the dark night of the soul as the negredo stage of alchemical purification, the water element as primary (hydrogen and oxygen are produced from water, not the other way around), the Earth as a hermetically sealed terrarium with a fixed water supply, the four element symbols and their correspondence to tarot and gender, fractality and hylomorphism as Aristotelian physics, and health understood through elemental imbalance where inflammation is excess fire and medicine is literally medi-sin.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Medicine Is Purified Salt for the Soul", "body": "Discussing the alchemical engraving titled Medicine to Cure Fantasy and Purging Folly with Drugs, Steve and Chance decode an image of an alchemist pouring sage essence into a subject's mouth while fantasies pour from his head into an oven's chimney. Steve explains that sage, from the Latin root shared with salvation and salvia, purifies both air and consciousness, and that the bottled virtues lining the image's shelf, like patience, humility, and counsel, are drugs named for the soul quality they restore. The insight lands: every drug, from table salt to ecstasy, is simply a refined salt carrying one quality of the soul back into balance."}, {"title": "Paracelsus and the Art of Concealment", "body": "Reading a dense passage from Paracelsus describing the Red Lion transmuting into the White Eagle, Steve and Chance unpack why alchemical writing hides behind circumlocution, talking around a truth so only a reader with the right heart can grasp it, protecting real knowledge from both the church and mainstream science, who agreed on nothing except their contempt for alchemy. They trace the Red Lion through astrology, as Leo ruling the heart, and through Jung, who read the reddening stage as the ego merging with one's true nature, while admitting some symbols, like the Green Lion, still resist a settled meaning."}, {"title": "Philosophical Mercury Is the Mind Itself", "body": "Working through the three levels of alchemical work attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, practical, theoretical, and philosophical, Steve locates philosophical mercury not in a flask but in thought itself: mercury's fluid, shapeshifting nature makes it the natural symbol for a mind that can picture a triangle, then a square, without ever touching matter. Vulgar mercury is quicksilver; philosophical mercury is the mental faculty that molds ideas the way mercury takes any shape it is poured into, with Chance adding that ancient Greek barely distinguished soul from mind at all."}, {"title": "A True Calendar Hidden in Plain Sight", "body": "Frustrated by the leap year's arbitrary patchwork, Steve traces it back to heliocentric theory and proposes the true calendar is the thirteen months of twenty eight days etched on the World Turtle's shell, a measure the sun and moon actually keep. The conversation turns to time itself: Kronos, the measured clockwork of heavenly cycles, against kairos, the subjective flow of personal, spiritual time that stretches a festival weekend into what feels like a month. Both agree the deeper epiphany is preferring quality over quantity everywhere, especially when quantifying something, like a day's length, destroys the very quality that defined it."}, {"title": "Mercury, Metals, and Buried Technology", "body": "Chasing how metals are actually made, Steve finds most are transmuted from rock through intensive processing rather than simply extracted, and that cinnabar, mercury's red ore, is wrapped in modern fear programming the way radium was quietly suppressed. He and Chance trade oddities: mercury dissolves every metal except iron, grows eerie crystalline branches when combined with aluminum, eerily resembling substances pulled from human bodies, and can generate voltage from atmospheric electricity spun through an iron bowl, raising Chance's speculation that the Dark Ages may have been lit by suppressed electrical methods rather than literal darkness."}]
